name: GitHub
summary: The easiest provider on the list: register an app in two minutes, no review for any scope. The only real decision is OAuth app vs GitHub App.

composio.note: Composio's managed GitHub OAuth app works today, so you can ship without registering anything. Register your own when you want your name on the consent screen or your own rate-limit pool.

capabilities.why: Any registered app can request it, no review

capabilities.label: Read & write repos, issues, PRs
capabilities.why: No review. Org owners may have to approve the app before it can see org repos

capabilities.why: Each org's owner has to approve your app (OAuth app access restrictions)

steps.title: Choose a GitHub App or an OAuth app
steps.detail: GitHub recommends GitHub Apps: fine-grained permissions, short-lived tokens, and they can act without a user. Use an OAuth app only when you need the classic `repo` scope model.
steps.agent: Recommend a type from what your agent needs to do

steps.title: Register the app
steps.detail: Settings → Developer settings → New GitHub App / OAuth App. Fill in name, homepage URL and callback URL (Composio BYO: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback).
steps.agent: Fill in the form and callback URLs; generate the manifest
steps.human: Click create while signed in and copy the client secret into your vault

steps.title: Get org owners to approve the app
steps.detail: Orgs with OAuth app access restrictions block your app until an owner approves it. With a GitHub App, an org admin installs it on that org.
steps.agent: Draft the approval request message for org admins
steps.human: Send it; the org owner clicks approve

steps.title: Submit a Marketplace listing (optional)
steps.detail: Only needed to be listed or to sell. Requires a privacy policy, support contact, webhook for plan changes, and more than auth-only value.
steps.agent: Draft listing copy, privacy policy and support page
steps.human: Submit; organizations only, for paid plans

Or register a GitHub App now. Nothing needs review to go live.
rejections: Marketplace: the app only does sign-in, with no integration value beyond auth
Marketplace: links to privacy policy or support are broken

blockers.problem: Users in an org can't see org repos
blockers.fix: The org restricts OAuth apps. Ask an org owner to approve the app under Settings → Third-party access, or switch to a GitHub App and have them install it.
A user or org can own up to 100 OAuth apps and 100 GitHub Apps. Reuse one app with several callback URLs per environment.

uncertain: Marketplace review time isn't published. The 1–3 week range is our estimate.
